The bill would change three areas of military law: the selection and independence of judge advocates, the handling of complaints about reservist protections, and minor updates to the defence discipline act.
It would let the Remuneration Tribunal set pay for judge advocates and require the Chief of the Defence Force to publish selection criteria for the Judge Advocates' Panel.
The complaints and mediation scheme for reserve members would move from regulations into the principal act, with a new compulsory conference option for disputes.
Gives the Remuneration Tribunal power to set remuneration for certain judge advocate roles.
Requires the Chief of the Defence Force to determine selection criteria and process for the Judge Advocates' Panel by notifiable instrument.
Creates the position of Deputy Chief Judge Advocate.
Transfers the complaints, investigation and mediation scheme from regulations into the Defence Reserve Service (Protection) Act.
Replaces references to 'prescribed person' and 'prescribed authority' with 'Chief of the Defence Force' throughout the act.
Requires an annual report on the administration of the Defence Reserve Service (Protection) Act to be included in the Defence Annual Report.

Members of the Judge Advocates' Panel, the Chief Judge Advocate, the Deputy Chief Judge Advocate, Australian Defence Force Reserve members, their employers and education providers, the Chief of the Defence Force, the Registrar of Military Justice, and the Director of Military Prosecutions.

The bill enhances the selection process and independence of Judge Advocates under the Defence Force Discipline Act, including extending appointments to five years and moving the complaints and mediation scheme for reservists from regulations into the Defence Reserve Service Protection Act, with the Chief of the Defence Force assuming complaint-handling powers.

The member supported the Defence Legislation Amendment Bill 2018, which improves independence and transparency of the military justice system by having the Remuneration Tribunal set judge advocates’ pay, extending their terms to five years, and clarifying termination provisions, while also strengthening protections for reservists by moving complaint and mediation schemes into the principal act.

The speaker acknowledged bipartisan support and contributions to the Defence Legislation Amendment Bill 2018, which includes three measures: amending the Defence Force Discipline Act 1982 to improve transparency and independence of judge advocates; moving the complaint, investigation and mediation scheme under the Defence Reserve Service (Protection) Act 2001 from regulations to the act; and making technical amendments to the Defence Force Discipline Act. The speaker also praised Australian Defence Force personnel for their response to the Townsville flooding event.
